scope: Read-only review of production Speeduino raw-logger comparison and native HAL. Source files were not edited. Only this requested review artifact was written.
verdict: PASS for the stated native digital diagnostic comparison. No unresolved functional blocker found. Does not establish whole-ECU equivalence, target capture timing or hardware qualification.

resolved_findings.description: Python bool/float channels compared equal to integers0/1, then were serialized as invalid IPC tokens and terminated the native child. C++ input parsing also used fields before checking extraction.
resolved_findings.original_reproduction: input_edge(10000,False,True), True,0.0,1.0 each caused RuntimeError and child exit2; rejected other invalid values left the child alive.
resolved_findings.resolution: Parent added exact-int channel validation and initialized/checked native input extraction before use. Source inspected after fix; independent five-test runtime suite passed.

evidence.plant_matrix: Prior14cases+4convergence report was inspected, not independently rerun in this review. This is separate from the digital logger comparison.

remaining_limits_and_test_gaps: Comparison feeds the shared project Capture.append ABI directly. It does not execute ESP32 MCPWM/GPIO capture callbacks, interrupt scheduling, synchronization primitives, pin conditioning or physical wiring.

Virtual GPIO and timers have zero CPU cost and no ISR jitter, missed hardware captures, capture-latch overwrite, metastability, analog behavior or electrical disturbance model. Preserving a3us virtual glitch is not a target resolution claim.

Only clean tooth interval parity is asserted. Production Speeduino tooth logging uses valid decoder-filtered trigger edges; the project diagnostic view derives intervals from all recorded raw crank rising edges. Independent noise/dropout tooth comparisons intentionally do not match. Raw composite fidelity remains the applicable claim.

Reference sync/cycle flag bytes are retained but not asserted equivalent. Independent probes asserted origin and simultaneous channel-level bits only. Project720degree phase/sequential support remains absent.

Default reference cam pin is disabled. The --logger-cam fixture changes production injection layout to sequential only to obtain a configured secondary interrupt. This is not equivalent controller-strategy parity.

Fixture resolves reference channels from current pinNumbers. It cannot validate physical Mega or carrier wiring. Official IRQ mapping was separately audited; asserting the expected per-case profile would improve regression detection.

The comparison final-RPM check alone does not prove continuity through a fault. Independent clean/noisy continuity fixtures strengthen the reference logger evidence, but remain finite ideal native tests.
The first reference tooth interval is excluded because its beginning precedes the project capture window. The next126 intervals cover common complete intervals and include later missing-tooth gaps.
Raw logger buffer access bypasses production serial framing. Desktop live TunerStudio acceptance and high-speed serial logger interoperability are unsupported; own ECU identity remains required.
No physical engine, HIL, ISR jitter, automotive EMI/surge, thermal, splash or printed-fit qualification follows from this review.
suggested_nonblocking_followups: Keep raw-composite and clean tooth-interval parity claims distinct from decoder-filtered tooth-log equivalence.
Add lifecycle and duplicate-level GPIO probes to the persistent reference regression suite.
Include project native-library binary hash and all transitive recorder/parser sources in comparison provenance.
Refresh stale documentation stating target raw capture is missing when publishing this increment.
Retain original plant fingerprints or rerun after parser-only adapter changes, so prior external-plant evidence is not silently presented as current-source evidence.
